root_motivation: PRD-agentic-memory §A item 11 (recall export / recall import) — round-trippable serialization of the v0.1 recall store as NDJSON. Closes the remaining standalone-buildable v0.2 item alongside recall-doctor (slice 1) and recall-ops (slice 2). Use cases: backup/restore, migration to v0.2 schema, manual editing in a single editable file.
user_persona: jsy backing up `~/.claude/recall/` to a single file for safekeeping, restoring after `~/.claude/` corruption, or migrating between machines. Output: NDJSON to stdout (one memory per line). Input for import: a previously-exported NDJSON file (or any conforming stream).

acceptance_criteria.description: `recall-io export [--root <dir>]` emits one JSON object per memory to stdout (NDJSON, one per line). Each object contains: `id`, `kind`, `subject`, `path`, `confidence`, `created_at`, `last_recalled_at`, `recall_count`, `embedding_id`, `supersedes_json`, plus the `body` (from the .md file, post-frontmatter). Empty store → empty output, exit 0.
Export is deterministic: sorted by id ascending. Two consecutive exports of the same store produce byte-identical output.

`recall-io import <jsonl-path>` reads the NDJSON stream, writes one .md file per memory to `<root>/memories/<subject>/<id>.md` (with frontmatter + body), and INSERTs rows into memories_meta. Creates the root dir + index if absent.

Import is additive by default — duplicate ids (already present in memories_meta) are SKIPPED with a stderr warning, original row + file untouched. Reports `{imported: N, skipped: M, errors: K}` in JSON mode.
`--replace` flag overrides skip behavior: duplicate ids cause the existing .md + index row to be replaced with the imported version.
Round-trip: export a fixture store → wipe → import the export → all ids present in memories_meta, file count matches, body content preserved byte-identically.
Malformed JSON lines on import → log to stderr with line number, count in `errors`, continue. Lines missing required fields (id, kind, subject) → same treatment.

Exit codes: 0 = success; 1 = expected failure (no candidates exported on empty store with --strict; all import lines invalid); 2 = invocation error (bad path, sqlite3 unavailable, --root that's not a dir).
`--format json` for import emits a single summary JSON object to stdout; text mode emits a one-line summary plus per-line warnings to stderr.
`recall-io import` from stdin works: `--` as the filename reads from stdin. Useful for shell pipes (e.g. `recall-io export --root A | recall-io import - --root B`).

scope: Rust 2024 CLI crate `recall-io` producing a `recall-io` binary.
NDJSON wire format (one memory per line).
Direct file I/O for .md read (export) and write (import).
Two output formats: text (default) + JSON summary.
non_goals: No SQLite linking (rusqlite); sqlite3 shell-out only.
No re-embedding on import — embedding_id and supersedes_json pass through verbatim.
No partial-export filtering (--subject / --kind / --since) — that's a query layer, not export's job.
No diff/merge — import is INSERT-or-replace, not three-way.
No daemon, no socket, no network.
Not the v0.2 schema migration tool (that's recall-doctor + recall-ops + recall-io combined, not a new binary).

five_whys_trace.q: Why NDJSON for export and not a single JSON array?
five_whys_trace.a: NDJSON streams. The store could have thousands of memories; a single-array JSON requires buffering all of them. Per-line shape also lets import stream and survive a partially-bad line.

five_whys_trace.q: Why include `body` in the export object?
five_whys_trace.a: The .md file is authoritative for body content. Exporting just the index leaves the body in separate files and breaks round-trip when the consumer doesn't have file-system access to the source store.

five_whys_trace.q: Why import is additive by default (skip duplicates) rather than replace?
five_whys_trace.a: Re-running an import shouldn't destroy in-flight work. The principle of least surprise: imports add, --replace explicitly opts into destructive merge.

five_whys_trace.q: Why a separate `recall-io` binary instead of subcommands in recall-ops?
five_whys_trace.a: Different concern: recall-ops mutates in-place; recall-io is bulk-transport. Pairing them would entangle two security postures (per-row touch/gc vs whole-store wipe-on-import).

ambiguities_resolved.question: What's the export `body` for a memory whose .md file is missing?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Empty string. Warning to stderr noting the file is missing. The row still exports (index row is authoritative for id existence).

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does import respect the subject directory hierarchy?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Yes. Subjects can contain `/` (e.g. `project:autobuilder`). Imported files land at `<root>/memories/<subject-with-slashes>/<id>.md`.

ambiguities_resolved.question: How does --replace handle a row whose id exists but whose path field differs?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Old file (at old path) is deleted; new file written at the imported path; index row UPDATEd.
